recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up core source edit is recommended for FHIR-11483 unless the Financial Management work group wants new, more detailed security guidance beyond the DSTU2 request.
issue_request: FHIR-11483 was a Published/Persuasive Financial Management change request raised against DSTU2 asking to fill in the Financial module's Security and Privacy section, with suggested considerations including billing codes exposing health-related information and financial information being a security/privacy target.
initial_application: No Jira-keyed implementation commit was found. The Financial module page was created in July 2016 with placeholder security/privacy text, and commit 4d97b6212a43b9561b83b29f7d66794a58c22fbe replaced that placeholder on 2016-12-01 with financial-specific PHI, claims data, security label/tag, authorization, and encryption guidance shortly before the recorded 2016-12-02 vote.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml lists source/financial-module.html as the active Financial module page, so the checked source is in current build scope. The current wording still covers the requested considerations by identifying financial/claims data as protected health information requiring clinical-data-level safeguards and by pointing to FHIR security labels, tags, authorization, encryption, and the general Security and Privacy module. Searches for FHIR-11483 and relevant financial security terms in Zulip and Confluence found no conflicting or later community guidance.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current source already satisfies the issue request and no necessary source edit remains.
